title: Two-storey column with beams: elastic critical load

source.work: McGuire, W., Gallagher, R. H., Ziemian, R. D., Matrix Structural Analysis
source.notes: input data and targets read on the cited pages; nothing of the source is reproduced

analysis: Plane (x-y) problem of the source modelled in 3D with the global Y axis vertical, so that the source's x, y and theta_z are the model's X, Y and rz. In-plane bending is about local z for every member (default orientation), hence the source's I is the section's Iz. a (0, 0), b (0, 6), c (0, 10), d (4, 6), e (4, 10) m. Column ab-bc: A = 2.5e4 mm^2, I = 6.36e8 mm^4; beams bd, ce (rigidly connected to the column): A = 1.76e4 mm^2, I = 8.61e8 mm^4; E = 200,000 MPa. a is pinned; d and e are on rollers that hold the vertical displacement only (as drawn in the source). Reference load 1 kN downward at c; the buckling factor is the critical load in kN. Linear buckling analysis. The engine's members carry the exact stability functions (no discretisation error for a prismatic member with constant axial force); the source's computed values use a stated number of elements with a polynomial (approximate) geometric stiffness. The source models each member as a single element. Plane stability problem: the source's model has no out-of-plane degrees of freedom. Here the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held and Iy = 1000 Iz, so that no out-of-plane buckling mode precedes the in-plane modes compared; J is a placeholder.

targets.precisionNote: printed "6630"; tolerance = half a unit in the last printed digit; computed by the source with one element per member and the polynomial geometric stiffness of its Eq. 9.14: an approximation by construction, no error bound stated
targets.sign: positive factor on a compressive load

quarantine.diagnosis: Source value is a discretised approximation; no stated error bound. Engine (exact stability functions): 6609.41 kN; printed 6630 kN (one element per member with the polynomial geometric stiffness of the source's Eq. 9.14); difference 0.31 %, tolerance from the printed precision 7.5e-5. Evidence that the difference is the source's discretisation error: a plane-frame calculation with the source's own element matrices (Eq. 4.34 and Eq. 9.14) gives 6629.6 kN with one element per member - the printed value - and 6610.8 and 6609.39 kN with two and eight elements per member, converging to the engine's value. (That calculation is a diagnosis aid, not a verification tier.) Buckling factors cannot be cross-checked by the foreign solvers of tier C.
